title: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review notes - 2026-03-14 (draft)
body:
Meeting: SRE weekly ops sync + reliability review
Date: 2026-03-14 (prep + notes)
Owner: Maya Thompson
Attendees (planned): Liam Chen, Carlos Rivera, Priya Nair, on-call rotation (Sam, Nina)
Drive-in: users/ (personal prep doc)

Purpose: quick weekly review of SLO health, paging trends, top incidents, and prioritized follow-ups. Keep it short (30-45m).

Agenda:
- 5m: Quick wins / shoutouts
- 10m: SLO snapshot and trends (last 7d, 30d)
- 10m: Paging trends / on-call feedback 
- 10m: Top incidents review (INC-5112, INC-5113) and mitigation status
- 5m: Action items and owners

SLO snapshot (quick numbers to bring):
- Hosted API availability SLO: target 99.95% monthly. Current 30d: 99.93% (delta -0.02ppt). 7d: 99.88% (due to two short infra blips).
- Dedicated pool throughput SLO: p99 tail latency for inference RPCs target < 300ms. 30d p99: 260ms. 7d p99: 410ms during nightly batch window on 3/10 (investigate).
- Console / control-plane API availability: target 99.9%. 30d: 99.91%. 7d: 99.85% (control-plane GC pause correlated with 3/11 incident).
- Error budget burn (30d window): Hosted API ~35% used, Dedicated ~12% used, Console ~28% used.

Notes:
- The Hosted API availability dips are short, high-impact for some customers (spikes in 5xx). Root cause appears linked to cross-region failover logic and a recent routing change (PR #8402).
- Dedicated p99 spike on 3/10 aligns with large background batch job on infra nodes; autoscaler mis-scheduled heavy work to inference hosts. Need better affinity/taints.
- Control-plane GC pauses: JVM tuning change rolled 3/9 (ENGOPS-842). Rollback reduced pause duration but we still saw one long-tail event on 3/11.

Paging trends (last 14 days):
- Total pages: 84 (avg 6/day) vs baseline 4/day. Increase primarily from rate-limited customers causing routing thrash and transient 5xxs.
- Top services paged: routing-proxy (36 pages), kv-cache (18), dedicated-scheduler (12), control-plane-api (10), logging-ingest (8).
- Recurring page: routing-proxy timeouts during EMEA morning window (03:30-07:00 UTC).

Top incidents (summary + current status):
1) INC-5112: Cross-region routing misconfiguration -> intermittent 5xx on hosted API (3/9 - 3/11)
   - Impact: 3 customer outages (short), elevated error rates for ~2 hours per event
   - Root cause: recent rollback of a canary routing policy left stale weights for EU region leading to overloaded gateway instances
   - Mitigation: temporary traffic shaping and rollback of the policy (done 3/11)
   - Next steps: add canary safety guard to routing service, automated rollback test in staging (owner: Liam Chen, due 2026-03-21)

2) INC-5113: Dedicated pool p99 spike during nightly maintenance jobs (3/10)
   - Impact: increased inference latencies; customers on Dedicated saw degraded p99 for ~3h
   - Root cause: batch job scheduler allowed heavy processing on inference-tagged nodes; autoscaler did not pre-scale
   - Mitigation: temporarily moved batches to non-inference nodes and increased buffer capacity
   - Next steps: enforce node taints and scheduler affinity rules; add pre-scale hook before large jobs (owner: Carlos Rivera, due 2026-03-18)

3) Minor: control-plane GC pause (3/11) - intermittent long GC causing control-plane API timeouts
   - Mitigation: rollback JVM tune (partial), monitor GC logs for next 72h (owner: Priya Nair, due 2026-03-16)

Open questions / discussion points for meeting:
- Triage threshold for auto-rollback of routing policy: should we be more aggressive? What are false positive risks?
- Pager fatigue: pages per on-call have doubled month-over-month for routing-proxy—propose moving non-critical alerts to slack digest and stricter alert thresholds for p95 vs p99
- Capacity planning: Dedicated autoscaler pre-scale policies for known maintenance windows/nightly batches
- SLO prioritization: do we need to adjust error-budget burn allocations for hosted vs console?

Action items (draft, assign at meeting):
- Liam Chen: implement canary safety guard + staging rollback test for routing service (linked ENGOPS-842). Due 2026-03-21.
- Carlos Rivera: enforce node taints/affinity in batch scheduler and add pre-scale hook for large jobs. Verify on staging. Due 2026-03-18.
- Priya Nair: monitor control-plane GC logs and finalize JVM tuning rollback decision; report back 2026-03-16.
- Maya Thompson (me): update SLO dashboard slides for exec sync (include error budget trend and top-3 incidents) and propose alert threshold changes. Due 2026-03-17.
- On-call rotation (Sam/Nina): run a mock failover drill for cross-region routing next week and capture playbook gaps. Target date 2026-03-20.

Notes to self / scratchpad:
- Bring the p99 latency graph for Dedicated (last 14d) and mark 3/10 spike.
- Pull PagerDuty export for last 30 days to illustrate page count trend by service.
- Quick demo of how routing weights test runs in staging (5m).

Meeting logistics: 30-45m slot, Zoom link (team calendar), record notes to Confluence page SRE Ops Weekly (link in linked_artifacts).

Status: draft. Will finalize after sync and move items to ENGOPS board.
